moonshot.tagline: Beijing lab behind Kimi and the open-weight Kimi K models
facts: Kimi K3 is an open-weight ~2.8T-param MoE, among the largest open models you can download
1M-token context, aimed at long documents and agent work
Kimi models are a common pick for agentic coding on other hosts too

crusoe.source: crusoe.ai header logo inline SVG (mark only, wordmark cropped)
crusoe.tagline: Vertically integrated AI cloud, from energy to managed inference
facts: Owns the whole stack: power generation, data centers, GPUs and the inference API
Builds next to stranded and renewable energy, including the 1.2 GW Abilene Stargate campus
Managed Inference sits on capacity it controls end to end, not rented GPUs

generalcompute.tagline: Inference cloud running on ASICs instead of GPUs
facts: Serves models on SambaNova ASICs instead of GPUs
Pitches speed and cost that come from the chip, not from GPU tuning

deepinfra.tagline: Low-cost serverless API for open-source models
facts: Among the lowest per-token prices for popular open models
Huge catalog: text, embeddings, image and speech models behind one OpenAI-compatible API
Simple pay-as-you-go, no commitments

openai.tagline: Frontier lab behind the GPT models, ChatGPT and the OpenAI API
facts: Serves its own frontier models: GPT, reasoning models, image, audio and realtime voice
The OpenAI API format is the one most other providers copy
The only first-party home for the newest GPT models

baseten.tagline: Inference platform for serving open-source and custom models
facts: Built for production: dedicated deployments of your own or open models with autoscaling
Truss packaging and its own inference stack tuned per model
Runs across multiple clouds so capacity follows demand

gmicloud.tagline: GPU cloud offering serverless inference and dedicated clusters
facts: Owns GPU infrastructure in the US and Asia-Pacific, a rare mix
Same provider for serverless inference and reserved clusters

modal.tagline: Serverless GPU cloud for running AI inference and sandboxes
facts: Run arbitrary Python on GPUs, not just a fixed model menu
Containers cold-start in seconds and scale to zero
Sandboxes for running agent-generated code are a big part of the business

meta.tagline: Meta Superintelligence Labs serving Muse models; maker of Llama
facts: Made the Llama family, which kicked off the open-weight model wave
Now serves Muse models from Meta Superintelligence Labs via the Meta Model API
Muse Spark Open is an 816B-param open-weight MoE (42B active)

openrouter.tagline: Unified API routing requests across hundreds of LLMs
facts: One API and one bill for hundreds of models from dozens of providers
Routes each request to a provider by price, speed or uptime, with automatic fallback
Its public usage rankings are a de facto leaderboard for what developers actually use

armada.tagline: Containerized edge data centers for AI where data is generated
facts: Inference at the edge: containerized data centers shipped to where data is created
Built for remote sites like energy fields, defense and mining with little or no connectivity

openscale.tagline: Cheap, fast API for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM open models
facts: Narrow menu, low prices: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM models
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at $0.06/M input on promo, at 200+ tok/s
Speaks both the OpenAI and Anthropic API formats

vercel.tagline: Vercel's single API gateway to hundreds of AI models
facts: A gateway, not a host: one key for hundreds of models across providers
No markup on tokens, even with your own keys
Built into the Vercel AI SDK, with automatic failover between providers

groq.tagline: Inference neocloud built on LPU and NVIDIA hardware
facts: Runs models on its own LPU chips, built for low-latency token generation
Known for very high tokens per second on open models
Licensed its tech to Nvidia in a ~$20B deal and runs 13 data centers
Offers a flat-rate plan (Wafer Pass) as well as per-token pricing
Fast open-model inference on NVIDIA B300s

inception.tagline: Diffusion LLMs (Mercury) generating tokens in parallel
facts: Diffusion LLMs: Mercury writes many tokens in parallel instead of one at a time
That makes it several times faster than same-size autoregressive models
Mercury was the first commercial diffusion LLM

mistral.tagline: Paris lab building open-weight models and sovereign AI infrastructure
facts: Europe's leading lab, with open weights under Apache 2.0
Mistral Large 3 is a 675B-param open MoE
Sells sovereign deployments for governments and companies that need data to stay local

thinkingmachines.tagline: Mira Murati's research lab; Tinker API for fine-tuning open models
facts: Doesn't serve a chat API: Tinker lets you fine-tune open models without managing GPUs
You write the training loop, it handles the distributed infrastructure
Research lab from former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati

cloudflare.tagline: Serverless GPU inference on Cloudflare's global edge network
facts: Inference runs on GPUs spread across 180+ cities, close to users
Called from Workers, so the model sits next to your app logic
Pairs with Cloudflare's AI Gateway and Vectorize for caching and retrieval

subconscious.tagline: Inference for long-running agents with 200k+ token sessions
facts: Built for long-running agents, with sessions past 200k tokens
Marathon versions of GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 tuned for long agent runs
Spun out of MIT research; OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API

morph.tagline: Fast Apply code-edit models and inference for coding agents
facts: Specialized models for coding agents, not general chat
Fast Apply merges LLM code edits at 4,500+ tok/s
Also offers WarpGrep code search and Compact context tools

cohere.tagline: Enterprise and sovereign AI models (Command) and the North platform
facts: Enterprise-first: models built for retrieval, tool use and business data
Deploys privately in your cloud or on-prem, including sovereign setups
Its Embed and Rerank models are widely used in search pipelines

stepfun.tagline: Shanghai lab building the Step family of foundation models
facts: Step models from a Shanghai lab, strong on multimodal and reasoning
Served through the StepFun Open Platform

infron.tagline: Unified API gateway to hundreds of AI models
facts: Provider routing picks which host serves each request
Passes through provider pricing with no markup, and supports your own keys

dolphin.tagline: Uncensored Dolphin models served on a network of distributed consumer GPUs
facts: Serves the uncensored Dolphin models
Runs on a decentralized network of idle consumer GPUs instead of data centers

parasail.tagline: Pay-per-token inference cloud for open models
facts: Owns no GPUs: rents across providers and passes on the savings
Pay-per-token open models plus dedicated deployments
Founded by Groq and Mythic veterans

venice.tagline: Private, uncensored AI platform on open-source models
facts: Privacy-first: no stored conversations
Uncensored open models for text, images and video
Stake the VVV token to get API access instead of paying per token

refuseless.tagline: API for uncensored, abliterated open models
facts: Abliterated open models with refusals removed
Drop-in OpenAI-compatible API, supported in LiteLLM

elevenlabs.tagline: Voice AI: text-to-speech, speech-to-text and voice agents
facts: Voice, not text: lifelike text-to-speech, speech-to-text and voice agents
17,500+ voices in 90+ languages, plus voice cloning
A top choice for realtime voice agents

fal.tagline: Inference platform for generative media: image, video and audio models
facts: Generative media only: images, video, audio and 3D
1,000+ media models, often available the day they launch
Its own inference engine tuned for diffusion models

anthropic.tagline: AI safety lab building the Claude model family
facts: Serves the Claude models: Opus, Sonnet and Haiku
Known for coding and agentic work; Claude Code runs on it
Also available through Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI

sambanova.tagline: Fast inference on custom RDU chips
facts: Runs models on its own RDU dataflow chips, not GPUs
Fits very large models like full DeepSeek on few machines
Fast open-model inference through SambaNova Cloud

boundless.tagline: Reserved, tuned inference capacity for open models
facts: Reserved, tuned capacity for open models rather than shared serverless
Runs on a ~4,000-GPU distributed network repurposed from zero-knowledge proving

runinfra.tagline: Agent that benchmarks and deploys open-model inference stacks
facts: An agent picks the stack: it benchmarks engines and configs, then deploys the winner
OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs with simple $1 credits

particle.tagline: Low-cost inference for open-weight models with 1M-token context
facts: Particle-1, post-trained from DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, with 1M-token context
Cheap: $0.25/M input and $1.00/M output

huggingface.tagline: Open-source model hub with routed inference providers
facts: Home of open models: the Hub hosts nearly every open-weight release
Inference Providers routes one API to many partner hosts
Pick a model on the Hub and run it there in a click

fireworks.tagline: Inference and fine-tuning platform for open models
facts: Built by the team behind PyTorch at Meta
Its own serving engine for fast open-model inference
Fine-tune, then serve the result on the same platform

sail.source: sailresearch.com header logo inline SVG (mark only, wordmark cropped)
sail.tagline: Open-model API with completion windows that trade latency for lower prices
facts: Completion windows: wait longer, pay less
Built for batch and latency-tolerant work like evals and data pipelines

relace.tagline: Open-model inference and apply models for coding agents
facts: Models made for coding agents: apply, embeddings and reranking
Turns an LLM's edit into a merged file quickly and reliably

luminal.tagline: ML compiler that turns models into optimized native GPU and ASIC code
facts: A compiler, not just a host: turns models into optimized native GPU and ASIC code
Open source, written in Rust (Apache 2.0)

suno.tagline: AI music generation from text prompts
facts: Music, not text: full songs with vocals from a prompt
The best-known AI music generator

xai.tagline: AI lab behind the Grok models, now part of SpaceX
facts: Serves the Grok models, with live data from X
Trains on Colossus in Memphis, one of the largest GPU clusters
Part of SpaceX since February 2026

cerebras.tagline: Wafer-scale chips powering very fast inference
facts: Wafer-scale chips: one processor the size of a whole wafer
Among the fastest tokens per second for open models
Keeps model weights in on-chip memory, avoiding the GPU memory bottleneck

together.source: together.ai touch icon colors + lobehub geometry
together.tagline: AI native cloud for open-model inference, fine-tuning and GPUs
facts: Research-driven: home of FlashAttention, with Tri Dao as chief scientist
Serverless, dedicated, fine-tuning and raw GPU clusters in one place
A broad catalog of open models, often added on release day

bedrock.tagline: AWS managed service for foundation models and agents
facts: Models from many labs inside your AWS account and its security rules
Claude, Llama, Mistral and Amazon Nova behind one AWS API
Adds Guardrails, Knowledge Bases and AgentCore for enterprise apps

google.tagline: Google's Gemini API and Vertex AI model serving
facts: Runs on its own TPUs, not NVIDIA GPUs
Serves Gemini and the open Gemma models
Long context, plus native image, audio and video input

typesafe.tagline: Decision models for software that report calibrated confidence
facts: Decision models that report calibrated confidence, not just answers
Built for software that needs to know when to trust a model's call

nebius.tagline: Full-stack AI cloud with GPU clusters and Token Factory inference
facts: Designs its own servers and runs its own data centers in Europe and the US
Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) after spinning out of Yandex
Serve open models or your own fine-tunes on dedicated capacity

inferencenet.tagline: Inference infrastructure and custom model training for AI-native teams
facts: Cheap batch inference on spare GPU capacity
Trains custom models for AI-native teams, then serves them
Started as Kuzco, a distributed GPU network

coreweave.tagline: AI cloud built on NVIDIA GPU clusters, with open-model serving through W&B Inference
facts: The GPU cloud the big labs rent: huge NVIDIA clusters built for AI
Serves open models through W&B Inference, from the Weights & Biases acquisition
Training, tracking and inference in one place
